page: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance engineered for workloads demanding an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU allocation. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8280M processor running at a base clock of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 38 MB of shared L3 cache and support for AVX-512 vector instruction extensions.

The defining characteristic of the M8-4ms is its provision of 219.0 GB of RAM, equating to 54.69 GB per vCPU. Storage capabilities include a 275 GB local SSD intended for temporary scratch space, swap files, and operational caching, with support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units, dedicating all host resources strictly to CPU compute and system memory operations.

Benchmark assessments highlight an architecture tuned specifically for high-capacity memory footprint rather than raw computational throughput. Across standard suites, the system records modest compute marks, with a Geekbench single-core score of 885.0 and multi-core score of 1970.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 3277.47. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 17.71 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth achieves 17.19 GB/sec. Redis performance reaches 2.63 million operations per second, reflecting the system's capacity to maintain sizable in-memory operational structures.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M8-4ms trades high compute velocity for extreme memory density per compute core. It is primarily suited for memory-bound workloads that do not require aggressive multi-threaded execution, such as in-memory caching tiers, large working-set data stores, enterprise resource planning modules, and analytics pipelines constrained predominantly by RAM limitations.
description: Microsoft Azure M8-4ms is a specialized memory-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8280M processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. Configured with an extensive 219.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers an exceptional ratio of approximately 54.69 GB of RAM per vCPU. An integrated 275 GB local SSD accommodates transient storage and paging needs, with no bundled GPUs. Benchmark metrics reflect conservative computational and bandwidth performance, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 1970.0, a PassMark CPU rating of 3277.47, and Redis throughput of 2.63 million operations per second. The server represents an asymmetrical compute-to-memory profile that prioritizes expansive memory allocations over processing speed, making it well suited for large in-memory key-value databases, caching systems, and enterprise data workloads requiring substantial memory footprints.
